source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Example of How to Trade a Reversal

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode, sides field says mirrored/same. Helpers: body(i)=|close[i]-open[i]|; range(i)=high[i]-low[i]; avgBody(n)/avgRange(n) = plain means over bars 1..n; ema(n); tick = instrument minimum move; swingHigh/swingLow(strength) = a confirmed pivot needing `strength` weaker bars on both sides; highest(x,n,k)/lowest(x,n,k) = extreme of x over n bars ending k bars ago. This chapter is a single running chart narrative (Figure 1.1, CAT 5-minute, not reproduced in the text) referencing numbered bars we cannot see; candidates below mechanize the general pattern each passage illustrates, not the specific unlabeled bar numbers.

candidates.name: TrendLineBreakBeforeReversal
candidates.quote: he always wanted to see a strong break beyond the trend line before looking for a reversal entry
candidates.description: Context filter: only consider a countertrend/reversal entry after price has broken beyond the trend line of the established trend by a minimum distance for a minimum number of bars.
candidates.pseudocode: trendLineBreak(direction=down, breakBars, breakTicks*tick) // close beyond the projected trend line (from swing pivots) for breakBars consecutive bars by breakTicks

complexity.reason: needs trend-line projection from swing-pivot detection, then a toleranced break test

notes: Brooks does not quantify 'strong break'; breakBars/breakTicks are readings.
Recurs constantly through the book; this file's occurrence is representative.

candidates.name: PullbackReachesEma
candidates.quote: The sell-off below bar 3 lasted only one bar and did not even reach the moving average.
candidates.description: A countertrend move is only significant enough to matter if it actually trades through the N-bar EMA; a pullback that stops short of the EMA does not qualify as a real test.
candidates.pseudocode: lowest(low, pullbackBars, 0) <= ema(emaLength) // bear pullback testing down into an uptrend; mirrored for bull rallies in a downtrend

complexity.reason: EMA plus a short window extreme

candidates.name: TwoLeggedMoveCount
candidates.quote: It was two-legged, which meant that there was some two-sided trading and therefore the bears showed some strength
candidates.description: Primitive: the move since the last opposing swing pivot consists of at least legCount alternating pushes and pullbacks (a two-legged move), each leg confirmed by an opposing swing pivot.
candidates.pseudocode: countLegs(sinceOppositePivot, pivotStrength) >= legCount

complexity.reason: leg counting needs swing-pivot detection over a variable-length window

notes: Used throughout the book for both pullback quality ('two legs down') and pattern context.

candidates.name: ThreePushesWedgePattern
candidates.quote: Because the bull channel was a wedge (it had three pushes), it was likely to have two legs sideways to down.
candidates.description: Primitive: the market has formed three sequential swing extremes in the same direction, each extending beyond the last, separated by pullbacks (a wedge / three-push pattern).
candidates.pseudocode: pushCount(direction, pivotStrength) >= 3 // three alternating swing pivots, each a further extreme than the last

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and extreme comparison across three legs

notes: Reused for 'wedge bear flag' (p105, rally bar 16-19 had three legs).

candidates.name: SecondEntryPullbackCount
candidates.quote: he probably would have shorted below bar 11, which was a second entry short
candidates.description: Primitive: counts the ordinal number of a breakout/pullback entry attempt in the current trend direction (Brooks's H2/L2 concept) - this is the Nth entry signal since the trend resumed.
candidates.pseudocode: pullbackEntryOrdinal(direction, sinceTrendStart) == entryNumber
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the second pullback's signal bar (mirrored for longs)

complexity.reason: stateful counter over prior pullback/entry attempts, which is itself pattern recognition

notes: This is Brooks's H2/L2 concept; what counts as a distinct 'entry attempt' needs a design decision downstream.

candidates.name: DoubleTopBottomPattern
candidates.quote: bar 16 formed a double bottom with bars 14 or 15
candidates.description: Primitive: the current bar's extreme is within a tolerance of a prior swing extreme within the lookback, the two separated by an opposing move, forming a double top/bottom.
candidates.pseudocode: abs(high[0] - swingHigh(pivotStrength, lookback)) <= toleranceTicks * tick // double top; mirrored with low/swingLow for a double bottom
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (pattern classification, feeds an Entry elsewhere)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection plus a toleranced level match

notes: Also covers 'double top bear flag' (bar 19 vs bar 13, p105).

candidates.name: TwoBarReversalPattern
candidates.quote: he would have shorted below the bar 13 two-bar reversal and lower high major trend reversal
candidates.description: The previous bar and current bar together form a reversal: the two-bar extreme is a new local high, and the current bar closes back below the midpoint of the two-bar range, signaling failure of the extreme.
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] >= highest(high, priorBars, 2) && close[0] < (high[1] + low[1]) / 2 && close[0] < close[1]
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the two-bar low (mirrored for longs)

complexity.reason: window extreme plus a two-bar comparison

candidates.name: AlwaysInFlipAfterSpike
candidates.quote: The two bear bars after bar 11 would have made most traders wonder if the always-in position had flipped to down, and most would have decided that it was indeed down by the end of the five-bar bear spike that ended at bar 14.
candidates.description: Concept: the market's assumed always-in direction flips after a sufficiently strong same-direction spike; needs a formal always-in definition before it can gate entries.
candidates.pseudocode: alwaysInDirection() flips to Short after a spike of spikeBars consecutive trend bars // alwaysInDirection is an undefined design-level helper

complexity.reason: "always-in direction" is a design decision, not yet a codable test

candidates.name: MovingAverageGapBarEntry
candidates.quote: a third entry for a moving average gap bar long (its high was below the moving average and it was the first pullback after the strong rally to bar 10)
candidates.description: Primitive: a pullback bar whose entire range stays on the far side of the EMA (its high stays below the EMA during a bull pullback) signals strong trend resumption and is bought.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] < ema(emaLength) // long version, on a bear pullback bar within a bull trend, bought on a stop above it; mirrored for shorts
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the gap bar's high

complexity.reason: single EMA comparison against the bar's extreme

candidates.name: NthPullbackSinceBreakoutCount
candidates.quote: it was the first pullback after the strong rally to bar 10
candidates.description: Primitive: counts which pullback (ordinal) since a breakout/trend resumption the current bar belongs to, for gating 'first pullback' / 'third entry' style setups.
candidates.pseudocode: pullbackOrdinalSinceBreakout() == pullbackNumber

complexity.reason: stateful counter across variable-length pullbacks, needs pullback/pivot detection

candidates.name: StrongTrendBarPrimitive
candidates.quote: The rally did not contain two consecutive strong bull trend bars, so the bulls were unable to regain control of the market.
candidates.description: Primitive: a bar is a 'strong' trend bar when its body is at least a fraction of its range (tails not restricted), used to grade follow-through strength.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && body(0) >= bodyFraction * range(0)

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic on open/high/low/close

candidates.name: AbsenceOfConsecutiveStrongTrendBars
candidates.quote: The rally did not contain two consecutive strong bull trend bars, so the bulls were unable to regain control of the market.
candidates.description: Filter: over the last lookback bars of a countertrend move, no window of countBars consecutive strong trend bars occurred in the move's direction, signaling weak follow-through.
candidates.pseudocode: not exists i in 0..lookback-countBars: forall j in 0..countBars-1: StrongTrendBar(i+j)

complexity.reason: window loop over a persistent per-bar classification

candidates.name: BreakoutTestOfPriorGap
candidates.quote: The bar 16 area was the breakout test of the breakout gap, which was the bull spike from bar 1 to bar 3.
candidates.description: Context: price returns to retest the location of an earlier breakout/measuring gap; holding that level confirms the level, failing it signals continuation of the newer move.
candidates.pseudocode: abs(close[0] - priorGapLevel) <= toleranceTicks * tick // priorGapLevel is a tracked breakout-gap price from earlier in the session

complexity.reason: requires tracking gap locations identified earlier in the session, then a level test

candidates.name: MeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: Bar 25 was a large bear breakout bar and was likely going to be followed by a measured move down, based on the height of the trading range.
candidates.description: Project a move equal to the height of the preceding trading range (or prior leg) from the breakout point as a profit target.
candidates.pseudocode: targetPrice = breakoutPrice - (highest(high, rangeLookback, 0) - lowest(low, rangeLookback, 0)) * measuredMoveMultiple // Exit when close[0] reaches targetPrice; mirrored sign for longs
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (profit target, taken at the market or on a limit at the target)

complexity.reason: needs trading-range height detection, which is context-dependent rather than a fixed window in Brooks's usage

candidates.name: GapMidpointMeasuringTarget
candidates.quote: the middle of the gap being the midpoint between the bar 16 low (the top of the gap) and the 27 high (the bottom of the gap). This could lead to a measured move down today or tomorrow.
candidates.description: A measuring gap's midpoint, combined with the move into the gap, projects an equal-distance measured move beyond the gap.
candidates.pseudocode: targetPrice = gapMidpoint - (entryPrice - gapMidpoint) // mirrored for longs

complexity.reason: needs gap identification and midpoint tracking from earlier in the session

candidates.name: BuyClimaxCountWithoutPullback
candidates.quote: Bar 9 was the third consecutive buy climax without much of a pullback (bars 1 to 3 was the first, and bars 5 to 6 was the second).
candidates.description: Primitive: counts consecutive climactic spike moves (each a mini-breakout without a significant intervening pullback) within the session; the Nth such climax raises exhaustion odds.
candidates.pseudocode: climaxCount(sinceSessionStart, maxPullbackTicks) == climaxNumber

complexity.reason: identifying a 'climax' spike is itself a design decision, then counting them consecutively compounds it

candidates.likely_existing_rule: SpikeWithoutPullback (V02-04), applied repeatedly across the session and counted

candidates.name: ExhaustionVsMeasuringGapClassification
candidates.quote: It was more likely to become an exhaustion gap than a measuring gap (it was more likely to be the start of a correction instead of a new leg up).
candidates.description: Concept: classifying a breakout gap as 'exhaustion' (trend about to correct/reverse) versus 'measuring' (mid-trend, expect a further equal leg) depends on context (climax count, distance from EMA, trend maturity) that needs a design decision before it is codable.
candidates.pseudocode: n/a - classification concept, not yet a test

complexity.reason: the classification depends on several context signals Brooks weighs subjectively

candidates.name: StopSizedToSignalBarRange
candidates.quote: Most bears would have picked a protective stop that was less than the number of ticks in the bar 9 buy climax bull trend bar.
candidates.description: Place the protective stop at a distance smaller than (or equal to) the signal/climax bar's own high-low range, rather than a fixed tick amount.
candidates.pseudocode: stopDistance = stopFraction * range(signalBarOffset)

complexity.reason: single-bar range arithmetic

candidates.name: PartialProfitAtPriorSwingTestWithPauseBar
candidates.quote: he would have taken about half off on the test if there was a pause bar. Since there was no pause, there was no significant profit taking
candidates.description: Take partial profit when price reaches a prior swing extreme (a test) and the current bar is a pause bar (small range, indicating a stall).
candidates.pseudocode: abs(close[0] - priorSwingLevel) <= toleranceTicks * tick && range(0) <= pauseFraction * avgRange(lookback)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (discretionary partial exit at a limit near the test level)

complexity.reason: swing-level tracking plus a bar-range comparison

notes: Partial-position exits may not map cleanly onto an all-or-nothing exit-pane engine; recorded as Brooks states it.

candidates.name: TimeOfDayReversalLikelihood
candidates.quote: Since major reversals often occur in the first hour or so, he probably would have shorted below bar 11
candidates.description: Context filter: major trend-reversal setups are more likely (and more worth taking) within the first N minutes of the session.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.Time(0) <= sessionStart + firstHourMinutes

complexity.reason: needs a session-start time reference

candidates.name: SpikeAndChannelDayType
candidates.quote: Since the day was a spike and channel bull at that point, the sell-off might have just tested the bar 4 start of the bull channel
candidates.description: Concept: classifying the day's trend as 'spike and channel' (an initial strong spike followed by a persistent, shallower channel trend) is a session-level pattern that needs a design decision (how to detect the spike-to-channel transition) before it is codable.
candidates.pseudocode: n/a - classification concept

complexity.reason: the spike-to-channel transition is a subjective read, not a fixed test

rejected.quote: Since traders are expecting a large move, the probability of success is often 50 percent or less... it can have a profitable trader's equation.
rejected.reason: general trade-management/probability philosophy, not a bar-level test

rejected.quote: Their denial causes them to miss the early entry. They then wait to evaluate the strength of the follow-through.
rejected.reason: trader psychology narrative, not decidable from bars

rejected.quote: Many bulls who bought between bars 10 and 13 held their longs through the sell-off to bar 16, to see how strong the bears were.
rejected.reason: narrates other traders' beliefs/intentions, not a condition the engine can evaluate from OHLCV

chapter_summary: A single running example (an unreproduced CAT 5-minute chart) walking through one day's reversal trade end to end. It mostly illustrates vocabulary defined generically elsewhere (trend-line breaks, two-legged pullbacks, three-push wedges, double tops/bottoms, always-in flips, measured moves, climax counting) via specific bar numbers we cannot verify, so most candidates here mechanize the general pattern rather than the bar-specific claim. The concrete, reusable additions are fading a large countertrend bar with a bar-height stop/target (V01-18, V01-14 companion), the moving-average gap-bar continuation entry (V01-09), and pause-bar partial profit-taking (V01-19); always-in, spike-and-channel day type, and exhaustion-vs-measuring-gap classification are honestly flagged research since Brooks gives no bar-level test for them, only discretionary chart-reading.
